name: Approach Velocity
rationale: Approach Velocity and Unflinching have very low pickrates and unintuitive functionality. The goal is to broaden them so more champions can use them, while also making them simpler so each rune is more understandable.
lines:
New Effect: Gain 7.5% bonus movement speed toward enemy champions with impaired movement within 1000 range. This bonus is doubled to 15% and does not have a range cap toward enemy champions whose movement you have impaired.
Old Effect: Gain 15% bonus movement speed when moving toward a movement impaired allied champion, or toward an enemy champion whose movement you have impaired. Range: 1000.

name: Ghost
rationale: Ghost has been a non-viable summoner for many champions for a long time now. Adding some power that emphasizes its strengths relative to other summoner spells with a sustained mobility effect for those using it aggressively.
lines:

name: Yorick
rationale:
R range for Maiden of the Mist’s leash decreased.
Making it so the Maiden leashes more responsively when Yorick exits a fight. We suspect this will be a small amount of power that skews towards the upper echelons of play where Yorick is currently weak.
lines:
Last Rites: Bug Fix: Mist Walkers are now able to properly activate Manaflow Band.
R - Eulogy of the Isles: Maiden leash distance reduced to 600 units from 900.

name: Ghost
rationale: Our changes to Ghost in patch 10.12 ended up being a small nerf with its increased cooldown, so we’re following up with a buff to speedily move it in the right direction.
lines: Bonus movement speed increased to 24 to 48% from 20 to 40%.

name: Anivia
lines:
Crystallize: Bug Fix: No longer applies the Aspect of the Dragon debuff on enemy champions.
Glacial Storm: Bug Fix: Storm SFX loop now plays correctly in Fog of War.

name: Ignite
rationale: We got some more VFX updates for you in this patch! Bring in the lucky contestants: Malzahar, Nocturne, Viktor, and Ignite (yeah, we know this is not technically a champion). Once again, our goals for these sorts of smaller scope updates is to improve the overall gameplay clarity of VFX whilst bringing them up to modern League of Legends standards. This means that our efforts are primarily aimed at abilities which do not clearly communicate their hitbox.
lines:
Updated visual effects.
Reduced overall noise while increasing clarity and timing.

name: Prototype: Omnistone
rationale:
Cooldown decreased.
Omnistone continues to significantly underperform, so we're giving it a buff so it has enough power to compete with the other choices.
lines:
Cooldown for melee champions reduced to 5 / 4.5 / 4 to 3 seconds from 7 / 6 / 5 to 3.
Cooldown for ranged champions reduced to 9 / 8.5 / 8 to 7 seconds from 11 / 10 / 9 to 7.

name: Nimbus Cloak
rationale: Nimbus Cloak’s popularity has begun to stifle rune choices, especially in the jungle. We’re weakening its power overall, with a specific target on its synergy with Smite.
lines:
Bonus movement speed changed to 5 / 20 / 35% from 10 / 20 / 30%.
Duration reduced to 2 seconds from 2.5.

name: Aegis of the Legion
rationale:
Epic items are the tier below Legendary: They're the mid-tier components of Legendary and Mythic items that build out of basic items. We're ensuring they serve their role as valuable building blocks, offering incremental stats and effects that smooth your progression toward bigger purchases. Like the Legendaries, we're providing blank-slate presentations of these Epics to give you a clean read on when you'll want to pick them up. New and updated have been mixed together since there aren't as many.
Like Legendaries, some Epics are getting simple tuning passes, based on how we want you to build into the new and updated Legendary and Mythic items.
lines:
Updated icon.
Recipe: Null-Magic Mantle + Cloth Armor + 750 gold = 1500 gold.
Stats: 30 armor, 30 magic resistance, 10 ability haste.
Builds Into: Gargoyle Stoneplate, Locket of the Iron Solari, Sunfire Aegis.
Recipe: Null-Magic Mantle + Cloth Armor + 350 gold = 1100 gold.
Stats: 30 armor, 30 magic resistance.
Builds Into: Death's Dance, Locket of the Iron Solari, Zeke's Convergence.

name: Infinity Edge
rationale:
Increased critical strike damage now scales with critical strike chance.
Infinity Edge is an iconic and valuable part of the marksman ecosystem, but buying it first most every game left little room for anything else to compete. We've reenvisioned Infinity Edge in a Deathcap-esque form that increases in value as a crit build progresses, allowing it to remain a staple power-spike in crit builds without defining the marksman early game with its awkward build path and lack of utility.
lines:
Updated icon.

Stats: 70 attack damage, 20% critical strike chance.
Unique Passive - Perfection: Gain 0.4% bonus critical strike damage for every 1% critical strike chance.
Limited to 1 Crit Modifier item.
Recipe: B. F. Sword + Pickaxe + Cloak of Agility + 425 gold = 3400 gold.
Stats: 80 attack damage, 25% critical strike chance.
Unique Passive: Critical strikes deal 225% damage instead of 200%.
Stats: 110 attack damage, 25% critical strike chance.

name: Rageknife
rationale: Giving on-hit champs the flexibility to access Guinsoo's new crit-converting effect without completing Rageblade itself so they can spec into crit chance items first if the situation calls for it.
lines:
New item
Recipe: Dagger + Dagger + 200 gold = 800 gold.
Stats: 25% attack speed.
Unique Passive - Wrath: Deal 1.75 bonus physical damage on-hit for every 1% critical strike chance, up to 175 bonus physical damage on-hit at 100% critical strike chance, but can no longer critically strike. Damage applies to structures.
Limited to 1 Crit Modifier item.
Builds Into: Guinsoo's Rageblade.

name: Rylai's Crystal Scepter
rationale: Some items are only being returned to fit into preseason-the biggest change you'll find in any of the sections below is the addition or removal of stat types, but not entire unique effects (with Mikael's' regen-granting Harmony passive as an exception). As with the other Legendaries, keep in mind that Mythic passives add additional stats that aren't listed here, so things that look like flat nerfs are at least in part adjusting for that extra power.
lines:
Updated icon.
Recipe: Blasting Wand + Giant's Belt + Amplifying Tome + 815 gold = 3000 gold.
Stats: 90 ability power, 350 health.
Unique Passive - Rimefrost: Damaging an enemy with an ability slows them 30% from 1 second.
Limited to 1 Rylai's Crystal Scepter.
Recipe: Blasting Wand + Amplifying Tome + Ruby Crystal + 915 gold = 2600 gold.
Stats: 90 ability power, 300 health.
Unique Passive: Damaging abilities and spells slow affected units by 20% for 1 second.

name: Time Warp Tonic
rationale: Small clarity update to Time Warp Tonic as the cooldown on consumables was occasionally confusing to players for a minor rune.
lines: New Effect: No longer puts the consumable on cooldown, if consumables are stacked the instant restoration is applied after the duration of the initial consumable ends.

name: Twitch
rationale:
Q attack speed increased. W slow increased. R bonus damage increased.
Both AP and AD Twitch are significantly underperforming. Our goals are for both to be viable ways to play him, but to stay true to his original gameplay design, we don't necessarily want his AP gameplay to be stronger than AD. For now, we're going to be buffing him in both styles of play, but it is possible that we will need further tuning adjustments as players get used to AP Twitch.
lines:
Q - Ambush: Bonus attack speed increased to 40 to 60% from 30 to 50%.
W - Venom Cask: Slow increased to 30 to 50% from 25 to 45%.
R - Spray and Pray: Bonus attack damage increased to 25 to 55 from 20 to 50.

name: Hailblade
rationale: Grouping some individual item changes since most of our item changes this patch can be easily categorized by class. A couple of notes on some specific items though: Muramana has started to see play as the optimal second item for several mage champions. We're changing its effect to physical damage to incentivize its target audience to pick it up (AD casters, where ya at), while laying the groundwork for potential buffs that won't encourage more mage poaching. And Seeker's Armguard was too efficient for its cost, so we're nudging down its power.
lines:
Enabled on Nexus Blitz.
Removed: Basic attacks no longer apply one tick of damage.

name: Singed
rationale:
Base health and armor decreased.
Singed was pumped up on his plant-based potion before it was cool. While his healthy libations have been letting him conquer the top lane, we're going to make his triumphs a bit more risky by reducing his early tankiness.
lines:
Base health reduced to 580 from 610.
Base armor reduced to 34 from 37.

name: Combat rules
lines: Slow resistance will now stack multiplicatively instead of linearly. As an example of the change, two 30% slow resistance effects will now reduce slows by 51% rather than 60%.

name: Lissandra
rationale:
Q AP ratio increased.
We're putting some power back into Lissandra's (cold) bread and (frozen) butter ability, so enemies know they can't just eat them willy nilly.
lines: Q - Ice Shard: AP ratio increased to 80% AP from 70% AP.

name: Conditioning
rationale:
Activation time increased.
Conditioning has been overperforming, particularly for tanks and fighters. It should be a little more costly to one's early power for what it gives in the late-game. Not only is it a fine choice for anyone, it’s mandatory for tanks and fighters, where it stands head and shoulders above any other single rune.
lines: Bonus resistance time increased to 12 minutes from 10.

name: Lee Sin
rationale:
E cooldown increased.
Lee’s buff in patch 11.8 shot him higher than anticipated in every role (jungle, top, and mid), so we’re partially pulling it back.
lines: E - Tempest: Cooldown increased to 9 seconds from 8.

name: Nimbus Cloak
rationale: As part of the mobility changes above, we’re pulling back on Nimbus Cloak’s bonus movement speed.
lines: Bonus movement speed reduced to 5 / 20 / 25% from 5 / 20 / 35%.

name: Smite
rationale: Challenging and Chilling Smite give junglers early access to true damage against minions, which is especially punishing to early ranks of ultimate-summoned pets like Tibbers, H-28Q Apex Turret, Daisy, and the Maiden of the Mist. We're adding a damage modifier to Challenging and Chilling Smite so that smiting pets can still remain as a strategic choice for junglers throughout the game, but they aren’t able to completely obliterate low-rank ultimate pets as soon as Smite upgrades. And a reminder: minions includes pets, but doesn’t include monsters—so monster damage numbers remain unchanged here.
lines:
Damage to minions and pets changed to 500 (+ 10% of target's maximum health) from 900.
Damage to minions and pets changed to 500 (+ 10% of target's maximum health) from 900.

name: Gwen
rationale:
E bonus attack speed decreased early.
Equipped with raw stat power and a big ol’ pair of scissors, it’s a little too easy for Gwen to snip back at even the toughest of opponents. We’re looking to sharpen her intended weakness by tapping down the speed of her slashes from level 1.
lines: E - Skip ‘n Slash: Bonus attack speed reduced to 20 to 80% from 40 to 80%.

name: Maokai
rationale:
Passive heal increased. E detonation damage decreased.
Top Maokai has been struggling to stay in lane even with his tank builds, so we’re increasing his sustain. On the other hand, Support Mao and his saplings have been causing a commotion in the bot lane, where AP builds offer powerful scaling. Maokai will still have strong poke, but we’re toning it down. One more thing: Maokai's original passive values were bugged. He was healing for less of his maximum health (5-13% instead of 6-13%) and it wasn’t scaling properly (it was scaling linearly at every level instead of its intended breakpoints of level 1/6/9…). so the previous values of his passive’s heal reflect the bugged, in-game values. Now, the scaling has been corrected, and the heal from his maximum health has an even bigger bump than his tooltip would have you believe.
lines:
Passive - Sap Magic: Heal health ratio increased to 7 / 8.5 / 10 to 15% maximum health from 6 / 7.5 / 9 to 13%.
E - Sapling Toss: Base damage reduced to 20 to 120 from 25 to 125.
E - Sapling Toss: Empowered base damage reduced to 40 to 240 from 50 to 250.
E - Sapling Toss: AP ratio reduced to 0.7% per 100 AP from 0.8% per 100 AP.
E - Sapling Toss: Empowered AP ratio reduced to 1.4% per 100 AP from 1.6% per 100 AP.

name: Divine Sunderer
rationale: Divine Sunderer has been the go-to choice for fighters all across the spectrum, and even some marksmen. We're looking to nerf its generic power to let its more aggressive item competitors outshine it when they're supposed to.
lines: Attack damage reduced to 35 from 40.

name: Predator
rationale: Increasing Predator's ganking power to push it up to Pro viability for junglers who gotta go fast—like former users Skarner, Hecarim, and Lillia.
lines:
Maximum bonus movement speed increased to 60% from 45%.
Bonus movement speed ramp up time reduced to 1 second from 1.5.

name: Rakan
lines: Base magic resistance reduced to 32 from 32.1.

name: Guardian Angel
lines:
Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where certain summoner spells could be used while in the resurrecting state.
Cooldown for summoner spells restored.

name: Lost Chapter
lines: Now builds into Crown of the Shattered Queen.

name: Glacial Augment
rationale: Some champions were using Glacial Augment's Freeze Ray to CC enemies before casting skillshots to guarantee a wombo combo, which—though clever—wasn’t the intended design. This updated version should appeal to tanks and some enchanters without removing skill expression. We think it'll be particularly useful to defend allies or amplify huge engages.
lines:
Immobilizing an enemy champion will cause 3 glacial rays to emanate from them towards you and other nearby enemy champions, creating icy zones that slow enemies within by 35% (+ 2% per 100 AP) (+ 2% per 100 bonus AD) (+ 5% per 10% heal and shield power) and reducing their damage by 15% against your allies, excluding yourself, for 3 (+ 100% of the immobilizing effect's duration) seconds.
Cooldown: 25 seconds.
Glacial Augment: Basic attacks on-hit slow enemy champions by 45 to 55 (melee) / 30 to 40 (ranged) for 2 seconds, which increases in effectiveness over the duration. This effect cannot occur on the same target more than once every few seconds.
Cooldown: 7 to 4 (per target) seconds.
Freeze Ray: Slowing an enemy champion with an item active creates a 600-unit frozen line in their direction for 5 seconds, slowing all enemies within by 60%. The Freeze Ray can fire upon any number of champions concurrently, and has no cooldown.

name: Lethal Tempo
rationale: Lethal Tempo is a little too strong for some melee champions. It's also failing to fulfill its attack speed fantasy for ranged users, so we're shifting some of the power from its bonus attack range for them.
lines:
Bonus attack speed per stack changed to 13% (melee) / 7% (ranged) from 15% (melee) / 5% (ranged).
Maximum bonus attack speed changed to 78% (melee) / 42% (ranged) from 90% (melee) / 30% (ranged).
Bonus attack range for ranged champions reduced to 75 from 100.

name: Azir
rationale:
Q cooldown decreased.
Azir lost the cooldowns on Nashor’s Tooth and thus, some of the wind beneath his wings. We’re giving him a lift by returning some of it directly into his kit.
lines:
Q - Conquering Sands: Cooldown reduced to 14 to 6 seconds from 15 to 7.
Arise!: Bug Fix: Soldiers now properly stack Tear of the Goddess Mana Charge.

name: Galeforce
rationale: Galeforce is outperforming the other marksmen Mythics, both in the “crit chance” space and for champions who can flex into Lethality. As such, we’re pulling back some of the power we gave Galeforce in earlier patches.
lines: Cooldown increased to 90 seconds from 60.

name: Sunfire Aegis
rationale: We’re lowering the cost of some of the utility Lethality items to create a new division of 2600 gold AD items, both for AD supports and traditional assassins.
lines: Mythic passive changed to 5% tenacity and slow resistance from 5 ability haste.

name: Fleet Footwork
rationale: Although useful on a number of champions, this rune is a bit too generous with its sustain for AP champions, so we’re targeting that.
lines: AP ratio reduced to 20% AP from 30% AP.

name: Smite
rationale: Alongside Gromp’s buff and the hit to Ravenous Hunter, we’re adding an extra healing bump by giving some base healing to make it less treacherous for the junglers who are less tanky and struggle to sustain themselves.
lines: Base heal increased to 90 from 70.

name: Teleport
rationale: Addressing unintuitive and frustrating scenarios around Teleport, such as Teleporting and zooming right back into lane after an early death. In compensation, we’re giving it a buff to maintain its power as a playmaking tool.
lines:
Bonus movement speed increased to 50% at all levels from 30 / 40 / 50%.
Cooldown reduced to 420 to 210 seconds from 420 to 240.
New Effect: Now removes homestart and homeguard bonus movement speed.
Bug Fix: Formatting and vocabulary in the in-game tooltip changed.

Attack damage increased to 350 / 370 / 390 / 410 / 430 / 450 / 470 / 490 / 510 / 520 from 285 / 300 / 315 / 330 / 345 / 360 / 375 / 390 / 405 / 420 / 435.
Void Corruption base damage increased to 70 from 60.

name: Combat rules
lines:
Standard effect reduced to 30% from 40%.
Enhanced effect reduced to 50% from 60%.

name: Seraphine
rationale:
W shield and heal AP scaling decreased.
Seraphine's taken center stage as a result of the Champion Durability Update and her recent buffs in 12.12. While she shines brightest as a bot carry, her mid and support performances are also extraordinary. In order to help tone her down we're reducing how effectively she can support allies when itemizing AP by decreasing her AP ratios.
lines:
W - Surround Sound: Shield AP ratio reduced to 25% AP from 35% AP.
W - Surround Sound: Heal AP ratio reduced to 0.4% per 100 AP from 0.6% per 100 AP.

name: Staff of Flowing Water
lines: Heal and shield power reduced to 8% from 10%.

name: Scorch
lines: Damage increased to 20 to 40 from 15 to 35.

name: Sudden Impact
lines:
Lethality increased to 9 from 7.
Magic penetration increased to 7 from 6.

name: Mercurial Scimitar
rationale: Mercurial Scimitar hasn’t been as appealing recently given its role as an important itemization option that provides magic resist, critical strike chance, and a built-in cc removal effect. We’re increasing the benefits that come with this item to make it a little more tempting of an option compared to the other sword items carries can opt for.
lines:
Magic resistance increased to 40 from 30.
Bonus movement speed duration increased to 1.5 seconds from 1.

name: First Strike
rationale: First strike has risen to prominence as the go-to choice for burst champions in the current meta. We’re reining in a bit of its burst potential which should also decrease the amount of gold this Rune can generate.
lines: Bonus damage reduced to 9% from 10%.

name: Draven
rationale:
Q base damage decreased.
Draven has been an axe juggling terror in Elite brackets of play since his post-Durability Update buffs in patch 12.10. We’re rolling back the base damage portion of these buffs which helped him reach dominance in the bot lane.
lines: Q - Spinning Axe: Base damage reduced to 40 to 60 from 45 to 65.

name: Bounties
lines: Targets with an active objective bounty now have different health bars to indicate that status.

name: Gwen
rationale:
Q base damage increased.
Gwen hasn't been scary in quite a while as she currently needs to get into late game to start gaining an edge over her opponents. We're sharpening her mid-game power a tad to help her better compete with other, similar fighters.
lines:
Q - Snip Snip!: Base damage per snip increased to 10 to 30 from 10 to 26.
Q - Snip Snip!: Final snip base damage increased to 60 to 160 from 60 to 140.

name: Scorchclaw Pup
lines:
New item
Replaces Emberknife and Hailblade.
Cost: 450 gold
Unique Passive - Jungle Companions: Summon a Scorchclaw Pup companion to assist you in combat against monsters.
Unique Passive - Scorchclaw's Slash: Feed the companion treats to evolve it and upgrade your Smite. Upon the companion reaching its final evolution, this item is consumed, granting you the Scorchclaw's Slash buff:
Gain 3 Ember stacks every 0.5 seconds, up to 100. Killing a large monster grants maximum stacks. When fully stacked, your next instance of damage against an enemy champion burns them and all enemies within 250 units of them, dealing bonus true damage equal to 4% of the target's maximum health over 4 seconds and slowing them by 30% decaying over 2 seconds.
Limited to 1 Jungle / Support item.

name: Dragon

Stealth timer increased to 2.5 seconds from 1.5.

Base damage reduced to 25 to 50 from 25 to 75.

Champions taking hex-gates channel for 0.75 seconds, then upon completion blink to the other side of the gate over 2.25 seconds while vanished. They can additionally choose a direction to blink to 500 units away from the gate upon arrival.

name: Knight's Vow
lines:
Combine cost reduced to 400 gold from 700 gold.
Total cost unchanged.
Base health regeneration increased to 200% from 150%.

name: Hullbreaker
rationale: Ranged Hullbreaker users have been taking over top lane, so we’re decreasing its benefits for them. Hullbreaker should still feel like an option for ranged champs, but without overshadowing melee users.
lines:
Boarding Party bonus resistances for ranged champions reduced to 10 to 30 from 20 to 60.
Boarding Party minion bonus resistances for ranged champions reduced to 10*3 to 30*3 from 20*3 to 60*3.

name: Immortal Shieldbow
rationale: Demoting Immortal Shieldbow to a legendary item meant trimming its statline down somewhat. Shieldbow makes sense as a generically-accessible source of anti-burst for crit users, so it’s got an easy-to-appreciate stat profile of attack damage. One note of caution: Shieldbow is not meant to be bought early as its shield does not increase until level 12.
lines:

name: Teleport
lines:
Unleashed Teleport timer reduced to 10:00 from 14:00.
Unleashed Teleport cooldown increased to 330 to 240 seconds from 240.
Bug Fix: Icon for Unleashed Teleport is now properly updated from Teleport's icon at all times instead of only until exiting fog of war.

name: Duskblade of Draktharr
lines:
Nightstalker bonus damage increased to 0 to 20% from 0 to 15%.
Bug Fix: Nightstalker's untargetability now properly renders the user invalid to abilities even if they were cast before the fact

name: Jungle camps
lines:
True damage reduced to 10 to 75 from 10 to 78.
Slow for melee champions reduced to 5 to 20% from 10 to 20%.
Ability haste changed to 5 to 20 from 10 at all levels.
Bug Fix: Monsters no longer loop their animations while being displaced.

name: Malzahar
rationale:
E damage tick rate increased, minion execute threshold decreased.
In this patch we’re adding some small quality of life changes to Malzahar’s Malefic Visions to address some consistency issues with last hitting using E. While the lower minion execute threshold might look like a nerf, when combined with the faster damage tick rate this should result in players more reliably getting last hits on minions and that sweet, sweet gold.
lines:
E - Malefic Visions: Tick rate reduced to 1 per 0.25 seconds from 1 per 0.5.
E - Malefic Visions: Minion execute threshold reduced to 10 to 30 health from 15 to 45 health.

name: Nidalee
rationale:
E AD scaling added.
In this patch we’re looking to give AD Nidalee a little help in her cougar form so her swipes pack some punch. We’re not looking to make drastic changes to AD Nid, but just give her a little more support at the time.
lines:
Bug Fix: Several issues with voice line playback have been resolved.
E - Swipe: New Effect: Now scales with 40% bonus AD.

name: Bloodthirster
rationale: Bloodthirster is just slightly over-performing as a greedy purchase for winning players. It's proven to be in pretty solid shape for an item and we're happy that players can't easily stack two shields in the same build, but it just needs a small tuning pass. The rule update here aligns it with Absolute Focus, which is nice for consistency's sake so that these effects both leave and return at the same time.
lines: Engorge health threshold increased to 70% maximum health from 50%.

name: Future's Market
rationale: Future’s Market is simply an overperforming rune and is being consistently picked by junglers, more so than any other role. This change should help balance rune options and very slightly lower jungle power.
lines:
Base debt reduced to 100 gold from 145 gold.
Debt per minute increased to 8 gold from 5 gold.

name: Dragon
lines:
New Effect: Dragons now have a patience bar and leashing range indicator.
Removed: Dragons no longer instantly reset aggression once they leave their leash range.

name: Kayn
rationale:
Passive Darkin healing adjusted. Darkin R damage decreased.
Last patch we attempted to nerf both Shadow Assassin and Darkin Kayn. While his numbers went down, we also buffed one of Darkin Kayn’s key items, which means we only achieved our goals on one of his two forms. This patch, we're making good on our goals to weaken his Darkin form. It's worth noting that a Kayn who's doing well transforms around level 8, and the old version of his Darkin passive scaled from level 1. This change makes the healing more clear and ultimately nerfs his late game.

A 10% cheaper Randuin's Omen (now matching many other tank legendaries) should make it best in slot when critical strikes are the primary damage you're receiving without it becoming the default tank armor item.

name: Fleet Footwork
rationale: While most of the changes we've talked about thus far target gold access, these adjustments target how effective gold is in the rune system. The goal is to reduce snowballing by decreasing gold scaling through the rune system, as players already get plenty of power from item and experience leads, not to mention the ratios on these runes are more of a hidden power. Even though our main intention is to reduce snowballing, a secondary goal of these adjustments is to reduce the amount of damage in League. Our approach to these changes was to increase the base values of these Runes so that they are still reasonably impactful early game, but have them start to fall off once more items and other means of damage are purchased.

name: Forbidden Idol
rationale: We're broadly nerfing most completed items with a few primary goals in mind: First, we'd like to overall slow down the pace of combat in the late game. This pace reduction should be felt in actual speed, such as move speed and ability haste but also in burst damage for those classes who aren't centered around dealing significant damage in the first place. Second, we want to reduce the rate of snowballing, as gold is the primary vector through which winning teams grow their leads, so games should feel closer for longer and for lanes to not feel quite so hopeless off of a mismatched first item spike. Third, we want classes to play out more distinctly from one another, which means that burst classes will be bursty but not so well rounded that they can also compete as DPS threats, while the DPS champions should have a much harder time bursting and champions whose strengths are indexed in durability will have to rely on that tankiness to do their jobs. We'll go into more context for the changes in each section but broadly we nerfed most legendary items between 5% and 12% of their total power, sometimes focused on bringing down one or two stats and sometimes compensating with others.

lines:
New monster

We’ve held off on buffing them as we didn’t want to inject significantly more overall MS into the game, but with a rework to Swiftmarch and some small changes to the other tier 3 boots, we’re moving the system to a place where the T3 boots can be made more competitive with other options.

name: Voltaic Cyclosword
rationale: Voltaic Cyclosword brings some cool Energized options to AD casters, but we think we can make it even broader by allowing it to open up the strict auto-attack gate that stops many melees from being good with it. We also don't love the slow effect, as it tended to trivialize a lot of the combat once players did manage to get into melee. With Opportunity removed, Voltaic should also be able to stand as the premier "upfront burst" item for AD casters.
lines:
Total cost reduced to 2900 gold from 3000 gold.
Combine cost reduced to 863 gold from 963 gold.
Lethality reduced to 10 from 18.
New Effect: Damaging enemy champions with abilities can trigger Energized effects.
Old Effect: Energized stack generation is increased by 75% for distance travelled from dashes, lunges and blinks, as well as while moving in stealth.
New Effect: When fully Energized, your next basic attack grants you 15 (melee) / 12 (ranged) lethality for 4 seconds and deals bonus physical damage equal to 9% (melee) / 7% (ranged) of the target's current health, capped at 200 against non-champions.
Old Effect: When fully Energized, your next basic attack deals 100 bonus physical damage on-hit and slows the target by 99% (melee) / 20% (ranged) for 0.75 seconds.

name: Arcane Comet
rationale: Previously, Comet was given a cooldown refund mechanic for damage over time and sustained damage casters. Now that Deathfire Touch exists, Comet no longer needs it, and can now better serve its original intended audience of control mages and artillery mages with a damage-per-distance mechanic that should be exciting for those subclasses to play with.
lines:
Base damage reduced to 15 to 100 from 30 to 130.
New Effect: Damage is now increased by 0 to 100%.
Removed: Dealing forms of ability damage no longer reduces the remaining cooldown:
Spell damage: 20%
Area damage: 10% per enemy hit
Pet damage: 10%
Persistent damage: 5%

name: Deathfire Touch
rationale: We are also making an adjustment to Deathfire Touch so that it now only deals magic damage to resolve an extreme synergy with Black Cleaver.
lines: Damage type changed to magic damage from adaptive damage.

name: Stormrazor
rationale: Stormrazor almost had its time in the sun earlier this year, but has ended up remaining second fiddle.
lines: Attack speed increased to 25% from 20%.

name: Role quests
lines:
Teleport cooldown reduced to 390 seconds from 420.
New Effect: Unleashed Teleport cooldown is now reduced by 30 seconds.

name: Vayne
rationale:
R Tumble cooldown reduction now scales.
Similar to Riven, we want to work on targeting the frustration around playing against Vayne beyond just her raw stats. Right now, Vayne ramps up a little too early and is especially frustrating because of how often she goes invisible. These changes should lessen her power spike at level 6.
lines: R - Final Hour: Tumble cooldown reduction reduced to 30 to 50% from 50% at all ranks.

name: Amumu
rationale: This update is aimed at reinforcing Amumu's Shuriman thematic and improving his gameplay clarity. We also tried to make it as close as possible to the style in his music video !
lines:
New visual effects.
New basic attack hit effects.
All skins cleaned up to match the new effects on the base skin.
Cursed Touch: Cleaned up existing effects.
Bandage Toss: Added a subtle effect to show the width of his missile and brightened the tip of it.
Despair: Now displays a reflection and has a better representation of the hitbox.
Despair: New, more condensed impact effect.
Tantrum: New AoE, now with sand, and a better representation of the hitbox.
Curse of the Sad Mummy: More sand and actual Shuriman runes.
New, robot-y effects across all his abilities.

name: Sivir
rationale:
Champion hits don't reduce Q's damage.
Buffing the dream Q that hits all five enemy champions in a teamfight.
lines:
Q - Boomerang Blade: Hitting an enemy champion no longer decreases Boomerang Blade's damage against subsequent targets.
Ricochet: Undocumented: AD ratio increased to 55 to 75% AD from 50 to 70% AD
On the Hunt: New Effect: Ability icon HUD now shows the remaining duration of the ability.

name: Shield Bash
lines: Base damage increased to 5 to 30 from 4 to 21.

name: Turrets
lines:
New Effect: Champions within 2500 range who assisted in a turret takedown now also count toward turret gold distribution, including first turret bonus.
Turret local gold proximity radius increased to 1200 from 1000.

name: Ivern
lines:
Rootcaller: New Effect: Ivern now dashes to 125 range away from the target.
Rootcaller: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where he would land inside some jungle camps when dashing with his Q.
Rootcaller: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where allies would teleport to unexpected locations when he would dash to a rooted target.

name: Banshee's Veil
lines:
Unique passive is now named Spell Shield.
New spell shield VFX.

name: Ohmwrecker
rationale: Ohmwrecker's been underused and underpowered for a long time. Turret disabling is an interesting mechanic we think could have a place in League, but not one that potentially shows up in every team's toolkit, which is the risk a good version of Ohmwrecker presents.
lines:
Removed
Removed from the game.

name: Fleet Footwork
lines:
Energized stacks per attack reduced to 6 from 12.
Energized stacks per movement increased to (1 for every 25 units) from (1 for every 30 units).
New Effect: Energized effects now always work on turrets.

name: Presence of Mind
rationale:
Increases mana or energy pool on takedown instead of refunding ult cooldown. Now restores energy in addition to mana.
This rune's ult cooldown refund overlaps too much with Cloud Drake's new buff. Admittedly, so does Ultimate Hunter, but Hunter is usable by more champions and has a clearer goal, so it's the one that gets to stay. We're changing Presence of Mind to finally open it up to energy users and grant a resource pool increase (big brain getting bigger) rather than a partial ult reset.
lines:
Removed: No longer refunds 10% of your ultimate's maximum cooldown on takedown.
New Effect: Now also restores 20% of your maximum energy on takedown.
New Effect: Now grants 100 maximum mana or 10 maximum energy on takedown, stacking up to 5 times.

name: Map
lines:
New alcoves have been carved into the outer corners of top and bot lanes.
Bot lane now has three brush patches, instead of two long patches, mirroring top lane.
New brush has been added by the river entrances in both Blue buff quadrants.

name: Rift Herald
lines:
Spawn time reduced to 8:00 from 10:00.
New Effect: Can now respawn after 6 minutes.
Health changed to 8250 to 16500 from 10000 to 16000 / 16000 / 16000 / 16000 / 16000 / 16000 / 16000.
Base attack speed reduced to 0.4 from 0.5.
Eye of the Herald pick-up window reduced to 20 seconds from 40.
Undocumented: Eye of the Herald Herald's Call changed to a 1-second cast time from a 4-second channel.
Summoned Rift Herald level is now determined on picking up the Eye of the Herald, rather than on using the Eye of the Herald.
Summoned Rift Herald health changed to 3180 to 6360 from 4000 to 6400.
Headbutt turret damage changed to 1500 to 2250 from (40% of Herald's current health or 1500, whichever is greater).
Headbutt self damage increased to 66% of Herald's curent health from 25%.

name: Turrets
lines:
Icon updated to Ohmwrecker's icon, instead of Skull Crusher's icon.
Turret Plating resistances per stack increased to 0 / 0 / 25 to 130 from 0 / 0 to 100.

name: Shaco
rationale:
E damage ratio decreased; cost flattened.
Shaco is overperforming across the board in all his roles (AD jungler, AP jungler, AP support). Looking to bring him down a bit.
lines:
E - Two-Shiv Poison: AD ratio reduced to 70% bonus AD from 80% bonus AD.
E - Two-Shiv Poison: AP ratio reduced to 55% AP from 60% AP.
E - Two-Shiv Poison: Mana cost changed to 65 at all ranks from 50 to 70.

name: Sunfire Cape
rationale:
Cost decreased.
Despite its historical place in many tank and fighter builds, Sunfire Cape isn't showing up in many inventories these days. Making it cheaper provides earlier access to the full-powered Immolate effect, giving core users a leg up in lane and reopening the door to Sunfire builds for champs who've rotated onto other first items.
lines:
Total cost reduced to 2750 gold from 2900 gold.
Combine cost reduced to 650 gold from 800 gold.

name: Smite
lines:
Total damage reduced to 48 to 125 from 60 to 162.
Damage over time duration reduced to 2.5 seconds from 3.
Removed: No longer grants vision for the mark duration.

name: Archangel's Staff
lines: New Effect: Can now only purchase one Awe item.

name: The Dark Seal
rationale:
Ability power, sell-back value decreased.
Dark Seal is meant to be a greedy purchase to eventually upgrade into an even greedier Soulstealer, but its stat efficiency is so high and its sell-back value so good it’s become the correct choice to buy (sometimes in multiples) in too many situations.
lines:
Ability power reduced to 10 from 15.
Sellback value reduced to 140 gold from 245 gold.

name: Aftershock
rationale:
Resistances no longer scale with level; now scale with other bonus resistances up to a level-based cap. Damage no longer scales with AD or AP.
Aftershock is taken by a fairly wide variety of champions, especially those with access to hard CC who opt into this rune for a windowed boost of durability. Right now, it looks to be strongest on mages specifically: that extreme durability in combination with high amounts of burst damage mages can provide via Aftershock's AP ratio leaves little room for opponents to play against Aftershock mages. To combat these cases, we're specifically targeting Aftershock's scaling to better hit the same power level for all its users.
lines:
Bonus armor reduced to 70 at all levels from 70 to 120.
New Effect: Now scales with 50% bonus armor.
Bonus armor caps while having (80-70)/0.5 to (150-70)/0.5 bonus armor.
Bonus magic resistance reduced to 70 at all levels from 70 to 120.
New Effect: Now scales with 50% bonus magic resistance.
Bonus magic resistance caps while having (80-70)/0.5 to (150-70)/0.5 bonus magic resistance.
Removed: Shockwave damage no longer scales with 15% bonus AD and 10% AP.
Shockwave damage health ratio increased to 4% of maximum health from 3%.

name: Ghost Poro
lines: New Effect: Now also grants bonus adaptive stats when your Ghost Poro spots an enemy champion.
